problem: The text says AH adds a MAC over the IP header and payload. In transit some IPv4 header fields change (TTL, header checksum, DSCP/ECN, flags, fragment offset), so the MAC cannot cover the whole header; it covers the immutable header fields plus the payload.
fix: Write: AH adds a MAC over the payload and the fields of the IP header that do not change in transit (version, source and destination address, total length, identification, protocol). Fields such as TTL and header checksum are excluded because routers rewrite them.

where: Section 1 and the figure (ESP tunnel fields)
problem: The list 'outer IP header, ESP header, encrypted inner packet, ESP trailer, ESP authentication data' never says which parts are encrypted, so a student can read the ESP trailer as being in clear. In fact padding, pad length and next header (the trailer) are encrypted; only the ESP header and the authentication data travel in clear.
fix: Write: the encrypted region covers the inner packet plus the ESP trailer (padding, pad length, next header). The ESP header (SPI, sequence number) and the ESP authentication data are not encrypted; the authentication data covers the ESP header, the payload and the trailer, but not the outer IP header.

problem: 'It authenticates the sender' is loose: the receiver learns that the packet was built by whoever holds the SA key. In tunnel mode that is the peer gateway, not the original host, and with ESP the identity of the original host is not proven.
fix: Write: IPsec authenticates where the packet came from at the level of the SA - in transport mode the sending host, in tunnel mode the sending gateway. It proves the packet was sent by the holder of the SA keys.

problem: The chapter says the sequence number is 32-bit and increments per packet but does not say what happens when it would wrap. The sender must never reuse a sequence number under the same SA keys.
fix: Add: before the 32-bit counter can wrap (after 2³² packets), the SA must be replaced by a fresh IKE negotiation, so the same keys never send two packets with the same sequence number.
